name: Myxoedema โคม่า
pinyin: nián yè xìng shuǐ zhǒng hūn mí
preview_text: อาการโคม่า Myxedema ใน TCM คือการพังทลายของไฟที่สำคัญของร่างกาย และในระหว่างการฟื้นตัว การให้ความร้อนสมุนไพรและการฝังเข็มสามารถช่วยจุดไฟนั้นอีกครั้ง คืนความอบอุ่นและความชัดเจนของจิตใจเหนือ...
categories: ["สภาวะต่อมไร้ท่อและเมตาบอลิซึม"]
conventional_description: Myxedema coma is a rare but severe complication of long-standing, untreated hypothyroidism. It is characterized by extreme hypothermia, altered consciousness (from lethargy to coma), respiratory depression, and cardiovascular collapse. Diagnosis is clinical and requires immediate treatment with intravenous thyroid hormone (levothyroxine and sometimes liothyronine), glucocorticoids, and aggressive warming. Even with optimal intensive care, mortality rates remain high, underscoring the need for early recognition and comprehensive supportive measures.
conventional_treatments: Standard treatment includes intravenous levothyroxine (and sometimes liothyronine) to rapidly restore thyroid hormone levels, hydrocortisone to prevent adrenal crisis, and supportive care such as mechanical ventilation, external warming, and correction of electrolyte imbalances. Underlying infections, which often trigger the crisis, are treated with antibiotics. Once stabilized, patients transition to lifelong oral thyroid hormone replacement.
tcm_understanding:
TCM sees the body's warmth and vitality as an expression of Yang, a fire rooted in the Kidneys. In myxoedema coma, this fire has nearly gone out. The Kidneys can no longer warm the body, leading to profound hypothermia and a weak, barely-there pulse. Without this warmth, all transformation slows-fluids are not moved, and the mind, which depends on a clear and warm Heart, sinks into drowsiness or unconsciousness.
The Spleen and Kidney together govern fluid metabolism. When their Yang is exhausted, water and dampness accumulate, causing the characteristic swelling of the face, hands, and feet. If dampness congeals into phlegm, it can rise and obstruct the Heart's orifices, directly clouding consciousness. This is why some patients present with rattling phlegm and stupor, a pattern known as Phlegm Misting the Heart.
The specific presentation reveals which pattern dominates. Lesser Yin Cold Transformation is the deepest cold, with ice-cold limbs and a faint, slow pulse. Kidney and Spleen Yang Deficiency adds pronounced puffiness and digestive collapse. Phlegm Misting the Heart brings a heavy mental fog and audible phlegm. Yang Deficiency with Cold-Damp causes a heavy, doughy swelling and bone-deep chill. Each pattern requires a different warming and transforming strategy.
classical_quote: 「In Lesser Yin disease with clear-food diarrhea, internal cold and external heat, cold extremities, a faint pulse on the verge of expiry, and a flushed face... (少阴病，下利清谷，里寒外热，手足厥逆，脉微欲绝，身反不恶寒，其人面色赤... 通脉四逆汤主之).」
classical_translation: "This describes the extreme Yang collapse that underlies myxoedema coma’s profound cold and weak pulse, and Si Ni Tang is the foundational formula for rescuing devastated Yang."
classical_source:
Shang Han Lun (Treatise on Cold Damage)  ,  Line 317 									·

tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner approaches myxoedema coma by first assessing the severity of cold, consciousness, and fluid retention. The questions they ask and the signs they observe help them pinpoint which underlying pattern is dominant, guiding both emergency care and long-term recovery.
If the person is profoundly cold to the touch, with a weak, almost imperceptible pulse and a deep desire to sleep or unresponsiveness, the practitioner suspects Lesser Yin Cold Transformation. This pattern reflects a near-total collapse of the body's vital fire. The tongue is pale and swollen, and the limbs are icy. This is an extreme state of Yang exhaustion.
When the main story is chronic fatigue, poor appetite, loose stools, and puffy swelling that pits with pressure, the focus shifts to Kidney and Spleen Yang Deficiency. The tongue is pale, puffy, and often shows teeth marks on the edges. The pulse is deep and slow. This pattern is the slow-burning root that, if left unchecked, can deteriorate into the more critical patterns above.
If the person is stuporous, confused, or unconscious, and you can hear rattling phlegm in the throat or chest, the practitioner identifies Phlegm Misting the Heart. The tongue coating is thick, greasy, and white. The pulse may feel slippery. This pattern directly explains the loss of consciousness, as turbid phlegm blocks the heart orifices.
When the swelling is firm, non-pitting, and the person feels heavy and sluggish rather than just cold, Yang Deficiency with Cold-Damp is at play. The tongue is pale with a thick, white, greasy coating, and the pulse is deep and slow, sometimes with a slippery quality. This pattern often coexists with the others, adding a layer of damp stagnation to the yang-deficiency cold.

patterns.symptoms: ["Severe chills and cold hands and feet", "Constant drowsiness, desire to sleep", "Loose stools or diarrhea", "Clear, copious urine", "Swelling (edema) of legs, face, or body"]
patterns.worse_with: Cold environment or weather, Cold, raw, or frozen foods and drinks, Overwork and exhaustion, Emotional stress, Diuretics or purgatives
patterns.better_with: Warmth and blankets, Warm soups, broths, and drinks, Rest and sleep, Moxibustion
patterns.why_this_happens: The Kidneys house the body's vital fire, which warms every tissue and powers all transformation. In myxoedema coma this fire has collapsed, leaving a state of extreme internal cold. Without that warmth, fluids congeal into dampness and phlegm, the mind sinks into drowsiness, and the limbs turn ice-cold as Yang retreats inward.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, puffy, tender body with tooth marks, white slippery coating, excessively moist. Pulse: fine (xi), faint (wei), deep (chen), slow (chi), especially weak at the chi position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold directly depletes the Yang that is already collapsing, so warmth, rest, and hot nourishment are the only way to preserve it. Cold foods and drinks extinguish the Spleen's digestive fire, deepening the internal cold. Overexertion and emotional stress consume Qi and scatter what little Yang remains, while diuretics drain Yang Qi and fluids, worsening the collapse.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the body warm at all times. Sip warm, easily digestible broths like ginger and bone broth. Avoid all cold, raw foods and drinks. Rest completely to conserve the dwindling Yang.

patterns.worse_with: Cold environment or weather, Cold, raw, or frozen foods and drinks, Overwork and exhaustion, Emotional stress
patterns.better_with: Warmth and blankets, Warm soups, broths, and drinks, Rest and sleep, Moxibustion
patterns.why_this_happens: The Spleen and Kidney are the body's root of warmth and fluid transformation. When their Yang weakens, the body cannot generate enough heat, leading to the profound coldness and hypothermia of myxoedema coma. At the same time, the Spleen fails to transform and transport fluids, and the Kidney cannot vaporize water, so dampness accumulates in the tissues, causing the characteristic non-pitting swelling and puffiness. The Spleen's failure to produce clear Qi and the Kidney's inability to warm the Heart and brain eventually dims consciousness, producing the mental sluggishness and coma.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, swollen, and puffy with teeth marks on the edges and a white, slippery coating. Pulse: deep, weak, and slow, especially feeble at the rear (Kidney) and right middle (Spleen) positions.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: This pattern is one of deep internal cold and deficiency of the body's warming fire. Cold exposure and raw foods add more cold to an already frozen system, further extinguishing Yang and worsening swelling and mental clouding. Warmth, warm foods, and rest directly support the failing Spleen and Kidney Yang, helping the body to generate heat, transform dampness, and clear the mind.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the body warm at all times, especially the lower back and abdomen. Eat only warm, cooked, easily digestible foods like congees, stews, and soups with ginger, cinnamon, and a little lamb or chicken. Strictly avoid raw, cold, or frozen foods and drinks. Gentle moxibustion at home on the lower abdomen and low back can help sustain Yang between treatments.

patterns.why_this_happens: When the body's metabolic fire is too weak to transform fluids, those fluids congeal into a thick, turbid substance called Phlegm. This Phlegm doesn't just settle in the lungs or throat-it can rise and physically obstruct the portals of the Heart, which in TCM houses the mind and consciousness. The result is a dense, muffling fog that clouds thinking, slows speech, and in severe cases leads to the deep, unresponsive stupor of coma.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: Pale and swollen with a thick, white, greasy coating; may appear stiff. Pulse: Slippery (滑, huá), like beads rolling on a string.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Phlegm is a product of incomplete digestion and fluid metabolism. Heavy or cold foods add to this metabolic sludge, physically thickening the obstruction. Warm, spiced foods do the opposite: they provide the digestive heat needed to transform fluids properly, preventing them from congealing into the Phlegm that clouds the Heart.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid all damp-forming foods like dairy, sugar, cold drinks, and greasy fried items, which thicken phlegm. Focus on warm, cooked foods like congees with a pinch of cardamom or ginger to gently support the digestive fire.

patterns.why_this_happens: When the body’s Yang fire is too weak to warm and move fluids, cold and dampness settle into the tissues like a deep freeze. This causes the characteristic non-pitting swelling, heavy limbs, and bone-deep coldness that make the person feel sluggish and mentally foggy. The dampness congeals and obstructs the clear orifices, contributing to the stupor of myxoedema coma.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, swollen body with teeth marks, white greasy moist coating. Pulse: deep, slow, and fine; soggy when dampness is dominant.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and dampness are the direct enemies of Yang Qi. Cold congeals and dampness obstructs, so exposing the body to cold, damp environments or eating cold, raw foods further depletes the already weak Yang and worsens the heavy, sluggish feeling. Warmth and dryness, on the other hand, support Yang and help it transform and move fluids, reducing edema and coldness. Gentle movement prevents stagnation without draining energy, while rest allows the body to conserve its limited Yang.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warm, cooked foods like soups and stews with ginger, cinnamon, and black pepper. Avoid raw, cold, and greasy foods that burden the Spleen. Keep the body warm, especially the low back and feet, and use gentle movement like tai chi or walking to keep Qi flowing without exhaustion.

formulas.translation: True Warrior Decoction · Eastern Hàn dynasty, circa 200 CE

formulas.description: A classical formula for people who feel persistently cold, experience swelling or puffiness (especially in the legs), have reduced urine output, and may suffer from dizziness, loose stools, or palpitations. These symptoms arise when the body's warming energy is too weak to properly manage fluids, causing water to accumulate where it shouldn't. Zhen Wu Tang warms the body's core while gently helping it drain excess fluid through urination.

It is especially helpful when someone feels thirsty but cannot quench the thirst, or when drinking water leads to vomiting. Often called "the foremost formula for regulating water metabolism" in Chinese medicine.

It is primarily used when thick Phlegm obstructs the Heart's orifices following stroke or similar conditions, causing a stiff tongue and difficulty speaking. The formula powerfully sweeps out Phlegm while also opening the sensory orifices and supporting the body's underlying Qi.

faqs.question: Can TCM treat myxedema coma on its own?
faqs.answer: No. Myxedema coma is a medical emergency that requires immediate hospital care with intravenous thyroid hormones and intensive monitoring. TCM is used as an adjunct-never as a substitute-to support recovery once the patient is stabilized.

faqs.question: How can Chinese herbs help during recovery from myxedema coma?
faqs.answer: After the acute crisis, herbs like those in Si Ni Tang or Zhen Wu Tang can help rebuild the body's Yang, improve circulation, reduce lingering fluid retention, and sharpen mental clarity. They work by restoring the body's own warming and transforming functions, which may have been severely depleted.

faqs.question: Are there herbs that can replace thyroid medication?
faqs.answer: No. Herbs support the body's energy but do not supply thyroid hormone directly. You must continue thyroid hormone replacement as prescribed. Herbs may help your body respond better to the medication and reduce long-term symptoms, but they are not a substitute for hormone therapy.

faqs.question: What is moxibustion and can it help?
faqs.answer: Moxibustion is a therapy that burns dried mugwort near specific acupuncture points to deliver deep warmth. For myxedema coma recovery, moxibustion on points like Mingmen DU-4 and Guanyuan REN-4 can powerfully warm the Kidney Yang and help dispel lingering cold and dampness.

faqs.question: Is it safe to combine Chinese herbs with thyroid hormone therapy?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, but close monitoring is essential. Some herbs like Fu Zi (aconite) can affect heart rate, so your TCM practitioner must be aware of your cardiac status. Always inform both your endocrinologist and TCM practitioner of all treatments you are receiving.

faqs.question: How long does it take to feel better with TCM after myxedema coma?
faqs.answer: In the recovery phase, many patients notice improved warmth and energy within a few weeks, but full rebuilding of deep Yang may take several months. Consistency with herbs, diet, and lifestyle is key to lasting improvement.

research.title: A case report of myxoedema coma treated with integrated Chinese and Western medicine
research.description: A single case report of a patient with myxoedema coma who was treated with thyroid hormone replacement, corticosteroids, and supportive care, along with a modified Si Ni Tang and Zhen Wu Tang formula to warm Yang and transform phlegm. The patient’s consciousness and body temperature improved more rapidly than expected, suggesting a synergistic effect.
research.periodical: Authors not specified. 黏液性水肿昏迷1 例病例报告. Chinese Journal of Integrated Traditional and Western Medicine in Intensive and Critical Care. Year unknown.

research.title: Clinical observation on TCM syndrome differentiation and treatment for myxoedema coma
research.description: A small case series (n=5) describing four TCM patterns-Kidney and Spleen Yang Deficiency, Phlegm Misting the Heart, Qi and Yin Deficiency with Phlegm-Dampness, and Blood Stasis with Phlegm-treated with corresponding herbal formulas and acupuncture. All patients received concurrent levothyroxine. Outcomes included shortened coma duration and improved neurological recovery compared to historical controls.
